original.excerpt:
[2/5, 1)**. Below the onset the same machinery is *strictly stronger than at n = 1* — at x = 7/20 an
entangled 2-copy input gives the exact value **1102933/9570000 = 0.115249007…** versus
d₁(7/20) = 13/132 = 0.098484848… (17 % larger, exact rationals) — so the n = 2 layer is genuinely
more powerful, yet it dies at exactly the same threshold 2/5.
original.context: The raw two-use first-order coherent-information coefficient is compared against a one-use coefficient at x=7/20. Capacity is normalized per channel use. The same sentence also asserts a common zero-crossing threshold.

witness.explanation: The comparison omits division by two and the entangled-family threshold is not 2/5.
witness.evidence: The comparable two-use coefficient is (1102933/9570000)/2=1102933/19140000, whereas the one-use coefficient is 13/132. Their exact ratio is 84841/145000, approximately 0.5851<1, so the two-use value is about 41.5% lower per use. The entangled family changes sign at the unique root in (0,1) of 19x^4-21x^3-14x^2+28x-8, approximately 0.3912977695<0.4; substitution x=2/5 gives 64/625>0, not a zero.
